title: On-call contingency catalog for degraded embeddings and RLHF regressions
author: Aisha Patel
content:
SUMMARY:
This document defines the contingency catalog, triage flows, runbooks, escalation matrix, status-page and customer-communication templates specifically for incidents that manifest as degraded embeddings or regressions introduced by RLHF (reinforcement learning from human feedback) tuning or model rollouts. It complements general incident playbooks by focusing on symptom patterns unique to semantic encodings and quality regressions in production inference.

SCOPE:
- Services: embedding-service (embedder-v1, embedder-v2), rerank-service, semantic-search, similarity-indexer, recommendation pipelines that use embeddings, and downstream model pipelines that rely on RLHF-tuned chat models.
- Audience: on-call engineers, ML engineers, product owners, SREs, customer success engineers, and incident bridge operators.
- Excluded: hardware-only failures (power/network), general latency-only SLO breaches that have no quality signal. Those are handled by standard oncall playbooks.

GOALS:
1) Restore customer-facing semantic fidelity within 60 minutes for P0 regressions (see severity table).
2) Provide consistent, evidence-backed customer communications within 2 hours of detection.
3) Ensure reproducible rollback or mitigation paths that preserve user data and minimize model drift.

SEVERITY DEFINITIONS (specific to embedding / RLHF incidents):
- Sev P0 (Critical): Large-scale quality regression causing >10% customer-visible semantic failures (document retrieval miss-rate increase, embeddings similarity drop, classification accuracy regression on monitored prompt-sets) OR production RLHF rollout causing hallucinations or safety policy violations. Immediate bridge.
- Sev P1 (High): Noticeable quality degradation for a subset of customers or models (5–10% regression on canaries) or indexing throughput severely impacted by embedding failures.
- Sev P2 (Medium): Small degradation detected by internal evals or telemetry; no immediate customer impact but trending.
- Sev P3 (Low): Investigations, tooling, or model-improvement tasks with no current impact.

OWNERSHIP AND ROLES:
- Bridge Operator (first-tier): oncall engineer from eng-sre. Starts bridge, runs initial hypothesis checklist, coordinates comms.
- ML Triage Lead: ML engineer responsible for the model family (embeddings/rlhf). Runs evaluations, comparisons, and produces evidence for rollback decisions.
- Runtime SRE: owns serving runtime metrics, autoscaling, and cache invalidation.
- Indexing Owner: owns the similarity-indexer and reindexing procedure.
- Customer Liaison: CS engineer who drafts customer messages and liaises with account teams for impacted customers.
- Incident Commander: assigned for P0/P1 incidents; rotates from senior SRE/ML.

EARLY DETECTION SIGNALS (examples):
- Drop in retrieval NDCG (canary prompt-set) by >7% in 15 minutes.
- Sudden rise in semantic-distance variance between persisted embeddings and live embeddings (KS test p < 0.01).
- Increase in rerank-service false negatives on golden queries.
- Customer reports: consistent incorrect recommendations, high churned query failure rate, or safety policy flags.

EVIDENCE COLLECTION CHECKLIST (first 20 minutes):
1) Capture timestamps for when alerts began (UTC).
2) Snapshot canary evaluation results (embed-canary-suite). CLI: curl -sS https://embedder/api/v1/canary | jq .results > canary.json
3) Export sample inputs (redact PII) and their live embeddings and historical embeddings.
4) Check model and artifact versions: model-id, weights-hash, tokenizer version, quantization profile.
5) Confirm deployment events in CI/CD: recent rollout IDs from deployment-service.
6) Check inference logs for increased error rates, timeouts, or OOMs.
7) Validate KV cache state and prefix-hits: cache-hit ratio drop may surface changed embedding dimensionality or hash mismatch.
8) Verify indexer health: pending reindex backlog, failed shards, or index version mismatch.

DECISION LADDERS (triage -> remediation):
- If median canary score falls by >8% and rollout ID matches a recent model promotion -> trig rollback to previous model variant.
- If mismatch between tokenizer/token-version -> hotfix: toggle fallback tokenizer path and invalidate affected cache prefixes.
- If indexer backlog is high and embedding generation is healthy -> scale indexer, queue backfill, and post temporary advisory to customers.
- If regression only appears in RLHF conversations (hallucinations/safety flags) -> disable RLHF tuning flag for the model (config toggle) and revert to supervised baseline.

MITIGATION RUNBOOKS (ordered quick-actions):
1) Immediate containment (performed by Bridge Operator):
   - Add incident tag to service: curl -X POST https://infra/api/tag -d '{"service":"embedding-service","incident":"IN-XXXX"}'
   - Pin traffic to previous model variant via routing override: api gateway -> set route weight 100% to model:vX
   - Bump canary evaluation cadence to 1/min for 30 minutes.
2) Reproduction (performed by ML Triage Lead):
   - Run embed-canary-suite against model:vX (live) and model:vX-1 (baseline). Command: ./tools/run_canary --suite embed-canary --model model:vX --out out_vX.json
   - Compute similarity deltas and annotate failing queries.
3) Rollback (if decision ladder triggers):
   - Submit rollback via deployment-service with pre-filled template: rollback-template.json.
   - Revalidate indexer after rollback by running a 1% sample reindex and verifying NDCG.
4) Temporary customer shielding (if immediate rollback impossible):
   - Route affected customers to a compatibility layer (feature-flagged local fallback) that serves cached embeddings for frequently-seen queries.
   - Apply per-tenant throttles to limit noisy traffic contributing to indexer backlog.
5) Long-term remediation:
   - Post-incident: add new regression tests, extend canary prompt-sets, retrain with targeted human feedback, and adjust RLHF reward shaping to reduce regressions.

ESCALATION MATRIX (summary):
- T+0–15m: Bridge Operator + Runtime SRE.
- T+15–45m: Add ML Triage Lead and Indexing Owner.
- T+45–120m: Escalate to Incident Commander and Product Owner; draft customer comm.
- >120m: Executive notification and cross-functional war room.

STATUS PAGE TEMPLATES (short and actionable):
- Short public status (1–2 sentence):
  "We are investigating reports of degraded search and recommendation results for some customers. Some requests may return less relevant results. Our engineers are triaging; updates at 1-hour cadence."

- Expanded public update (situation + mitigation):
  "Update 2: We identified a model variant rollout that caused decreased embedding quality for a subset of queries. We have routed traffic away from the new variant and are validating baseline model results. If you rely on semantic search or recommendations, you may observe intermittent quality differences while we complete the validation. We expect an additional update in ~60 minutes."

- Internal customer-facing template (email for impacted customers):
  Subject: Incident IN-XXXX: Temporary degradation in semantic search/recommendations

  Hi <Customer Contact>,

  We detected a regression affecting the relevance of semantic search and recommendations for some queries. Our engineers have identified the likely cause (recent model promotion) and have routed traffic to a stable model variant to limit impact. We will follow up with a post-incident summary within 72 hours that includes root cause, mitigation steps taken, and credits if applicable.

  Immediate impacts: decreased relevance, delayed reindex for new data.
  Mitigation: traffic re-route, temporary use of cached embeddings for frequent queries.
  ETA for return to baseline: 1–3 hours (subject to validation).

  If you see specific queries that are producing incorrect results, please send redacted examples to <cs-team@redwood.ai> and we will prioritize.

  Regards,
  Customer Liaison

POST-INCIDENT ACTIONS (within 72 hours):
- Full postmortem with timeline, root cause, and mitigations. Use template: postmortem-structured.md.
- Add failing queries (anonymized) to embed-canary-suite.
- Create an alert-to-action rule: when canary NDCG drops >5% for 10m, auto-scale indexer and open a bridge.
- If RLHF tuning introduced a safety regression, freeze RLHF experiments for the model family until a safety review completes.

REPRODUCTION AND EVAL CHECKS (commands and thresholds):
- Run: python evals/embed_regression_check.py --baseline model:vX-1 --candidate model:vX --suite embed-canary --alpha 0.05
- Thresholds: if candidate median NDCG < baseline NDCG - 0.05 (5 points) -> fail. If p-value < 0.01 -> high confidence.

GAME DAY EXERCISES (recommended quarterly):
- Exercise A: Canary-failure scenario. Simulate a 10% drop in canary NDCG and practice rollback, comms, and reindex sanity check. Duration: 3 hours.
- Exercise B: Indexer-throttle scenario. Create synthetic burst traffic causing index backlog; practice flow-control, per-tenant shielding, and prioritized backfills. Duration: 4 hours.
- Exercise C: RLHF-safety scenario. Inject prompts that trigger safety flags in a canary RLHF model; practice disabling RLHF flag and rolling back. Duration: 2 hours.

ON-CALL ROTATION GUIDELINES (fairness + handoff):
- Minimum experience for ML Triage Lead: 6 months on the model family.
- Shadowing: new oncall engineers shadow three incidents (at least one game-day) before independent rotation.
- Handoff doc: outgoing oncall must provide: active incidents list, recent canary results, cache invalidation state, and pending rollouts.
- Fairness: block consecutive weekend oncalls to max 2 per quarter; implement a credits system for extra shifts redeemable for time off.

SLOS AND MONITORING RECOMMENDATIONS (concrete thresholds):
- Canary NDCG (embed-canary-suite): p95 >= baseline - 0.02 for healthy. Alert if 5-minute rolling drop >0.03.
- Embedding generation success rate: >= 99.5%. Alert if < 99.0% for 5 minutes.
- Index backlog: < 10k pending documents. Alert if > 50k for 10 minutes.

PLAYBOOKS FOR COMMON ROOT CAUSES (quick reference):
- Model artifact divergence (weights/tokenizer mismatch): rollback, re-run validation, tighten CI check for tokenizer compatibility.
- Quantization/precision bug: pin quantized profile in runtime and route to non-quantized serving while patching kernels.
- Inference cache inconsistency: invalidate prefix and rebuild for affected tenants, add schema version to cache keys.
- RLHF reward shaping regression: revert tuning batch and create unit tests for known safety prompts.

DOCUMENTATION AND OPERATIONS RUNSHEET (for Incident Commander):
- Timeline template (UTC):
  00:00 - Detection and bridge creation (who)
  00:05 - Evidence snapshot (who)
  00:15 - Preliminary hypothesis and mitigation (who)
  00:45 - Escalation decision (who)
  02:00 - Customer notice (who)
  24:00 - Postmortem draft (owner)

METRICS TO ATTACH TO POSTMORTEM (minimum):
- Canary NDCG time series with annotated events.
- Fraction of traffic shifted to fallback variant.
- Number of impacted customers and top-5 tenants by request volume.
- Time-to-rollback, time-to-recover, and time-to-first-customer-notification.

APPENDIX: TOGGLE AND CLI SNIPPETS
- Toggle RLHF for model: curl -X POST https://config/api/feature-toggle -d '{"model":"model-family-x","rlhf_enabled":false}'
- Query canary: curl -sS https://embedder/api/v1/canary | jq .results
- Reindex 1% sample: python tools/reindexer.py --percent 1 --index semantic-index-v2

REVISION HISTORY:
- 2026-02-15: Created by Aisha Patel (initial draft).
- 2026-02-22: Added escalation matrix and templates (reviewers: Marco Rossi, Elena Kim).
- 2026-03-01: Published after security review and small edits to SLO thresholds.

CONTACTS:

- Runtime SRE on-call alias: runtime-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
